chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ubaydullah al-Dihqan, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him), who said:

Three (types of people) Allah the Exalted will not look at them on the Day of Judgement; one of them is a man who takes Allah as a commodity. He neither buys except with an oath, and he does not sell except with an oath.
ai.seo_question: Who are the three people Allah will not look at on the Day of Judgement according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), identifying the first of three groups denied Allah's gaze as one who treats Allah as a commodity by relying exclusively on oaths for both buying and selling. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on sincerity (ikhlas) in commerce, warning against reducing divine invocation to a mere commercial tool for securing transactions. The phrase 'la yashtari illa bi-yamin' underscores the excessive and potentially insincere use of swearing by Allah to validate trade deals.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ubeydullah Al Dahqaan, from Dorost Bin Abu mansour, from Ibrahim Bin Abdul Hameed,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Three (types of people), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the Exalted would not be Considering them on the Day of Judgement – one of them is a man who takes Allah<sup>azwj</sup> with a commodity. He neither buys except with an oath, and he does not sell except with an oath’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Muhammad ibn Tsa from ‘Ubayd Allah al- Dihqan from Durust ibn abu Mansur from Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid who has said the following: “Abu al-Hassan, Musa, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘On the Day of Judgment, Allah, most High, will not look to three kinds of people. Of such people one kind is a man who does not buy or sell anything without swearing.’”
